x: Odde was second in the quarter and Gerry Trower won the junior 880 in good style and Ches Walker was also first home in the senior half-mile.
Mike Stearman was present to defend his 880 yards Junior title, but he was beaten by a newcomer to our ranks in Gerry Trower, with Bob Wolton third.
There were some Junior events on the programme and in these Gerry Trower was fourth in the 880, and in the 1 mile which was run in two sections, J.
Snoad, a newcomer to our ranks, ran a plucky race to finish second, and looks a promising find, while another junior in Gerry Trower gained third place.
Gerry Trower also ran well to finish 10th, with Doug Briggs 18th and George Stace 28th. Finishing places and times of our team were as under:—
Maclean, Gerry Trower and Doug. Briggs all close behind and with only four a side scoring, we thus had a hollow win in the team race.
Abbott, and they both ran very well indeed. Gerry Trower, although not liking the mud, also did well and our fourth scoring man was D.
Walker and Bill Lucas running for us in the two-mile team race, we gained an easy win, with Eric Herbert in fifth place to complete our team. Gerry Trower won the junior 440 and F.
Frank Kemp won the junior 100 and was second in the furlong, and Peter Hunt finished second in the quarter, with Gerry Trower in a similar position in the half-mile.
Casselton give us the lead, which was held by both Frank Kemp and Alan Law, but Gerry Trower could not match the strong finish of Hewson of Mitcham, and so we finished second in this event.
Gerry Trower was beaten by Boyd of Wallington in a close finish for the 880 yards in the good time of 2 mins. 2.4 secs., and Geoff Goode won the 1 mile in 4 mins. 41.6 secs.

Casselton was third in the junior 440, and Gerry Trower ran the race of his life in the half-mile, only to lose to Hewson of Mitcham, who did 1 min. 56.7 secs., and Gerry was clocked at 1 min. 59.4 secs., which must be the fastest time ever recorded by a club junior member!
